title: Thorn and Salt
premise: Freya Vane, a cartographer raised in the warded valley where magic cannot follow, discovers her late mother sold Freya's own soul to the Court Beneath the Mountain to buy the valley's protection. When the wards collapse and the stars go out, Freya must cross the unmapped wilds with a disgraced ward-keeper, a salt-witch exile, and a thorn-bound fox spirit who claims to know her mother's debts. As the moon nears its thirteenth turn, Freya learns the truth cuts both ways: her companions each carry secrets about the night of the sale, and loyalty demands she forgive what truth cannot excuse. In the court beneath the mountain she outbargains the Pale King by offering not her soul but her maps — every unmapped realm rendered knowable — and returns home to rebuild the wards with found family rather than blood price.
about_author: O. M. Okonkwo is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent a decade mapping coastlines before turning to cartography of the imaginary kind. They write fantasy about people who draw borders and the magic that refuses to respect them.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot Magic
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya finishes a map of the only world she's ever known — a valley whose border wards hum like caged bees — and finds her dead mother's ledger hidden in the map chest, its final entry reading 'one soul, paid in full.' Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath domestic routine.

chapters.title: Thirteen Bells at Midnight
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. On the night of the twelfth moon-turn, the wards shatter and every star in the sky goes dark at once. A thorn-marked stranger collapses at her door, whispering that something has come to collect. Emotional beat: terror and the vertigo of a world suddenly larger.

chapters.title: What the Fox Carried In
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The stranger transforms into a thorn-bound fox spirit named Bramblehoof, who claims Freya's soul was sold to the Court Beneath the Mountain — and that he carried the contract. Emotional beat: disbelief hardening into grim resolve.

chapters.title: Salt on Old Wounds
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef, an exiled salt-witch living at the valley's edge, agrees to guide Freya past the fallen wards, hiding that she once served the Pale King herself. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as gruff practicality.

chapters.title: The Ward-Keeper's Shame
chapters.summary: Dagny's POV. Dagny, the valley's disgraced ward-keeper, joins the party to redeem himself for the night the wards failed — a failure he suspects was no accident. Emotional beat: shame seeking absolution through duty.

chapters.title: First Steps Into the Unmapped
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The company crosses the border into wild country where geography refuses to hold still; Freya's cartographer instincts become their survival tool. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into vulnerability.

chapters.title: The Market of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. In a traveling market where identities are currency, Sef trades a memory for passage — and glimpses someone from her old life among the King's agents. Emotional beat: the cost of secrets compounding.

chapters.title: Bramblehoof's Bargain
chapters.summary: Bramblehoof's POV. The fox reveals he is bound by thorns to deliver Freya to the court, torn between his oath and his growing loyalty to her. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to war with obligation.

chapters.title: Rivers That Run Uphill
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The party navigates a reversed river canyon while pursued by the King's Hollow Men; Dagny saves Freya using forbidden ward-craft. Emotional beat: trust tentatively forged under fire.

chapters.title: The Salt-Witch Confesses
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Cornered by a former sister of the court, Sef admits she witnessed the original bargain — and that Freya's mother begged her to stop it. Emotional beat: betrayal, then the fragile start of honesty.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Mother
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Decoding her mother's ledger, Freya learns the valley's protection cost thirteen payments — twelve made, one due: her soul, on the thirteenth turn. Emotional beat: grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Dagny's Night of Falling Stars
chapters.summary: Dagny's POV. Flashback chapter: Dagny saw who sabotaged the wards — and it was someone inside the valley, someone still there. Emotional beat: dread of naming a traitor among neighbors.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Bramblehoof's POV. At a tollhouse run by a childlike oracle, each traveler must pay with a truth; Bramblehoof pays with the name of his thorn-master. Emotional beat: truths as tolls, intimacy through forced confession.

chapters.title: Hollow Men at the Ford
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Ambushed at a ford, the party barely escapes when Sef unleashes court-magic she swore off, revealing how deep her old training runs. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by fear of what Sef can become.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Door
chapters.summary: Dagny's POV. The party realizes the saboteur will meet them at the mountain's gate — and Dagny must decide whether to warn or confront them alone. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against justice.

chapters.title: Descent Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. They enter the Court Beneath the Mountain, a palace carved from starless geode, where the missing stars hang caged as chandeliers. Emotional beat: wonder weaponized into menace.

chapters.title: Audience with the Pale King
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The Pale King offers Freya comfort, power, belonging — everything the valley never gave her — if she surrenders willingly. Emotional beat: temptation striking at her deepest wound.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The moon completes its turn; the contract activates. Bramblehoof breaks his thorn-oath to shield Freya, and Sef turns her court-training against the King's guards. Emotional beat: sacrifice as proof of family chosen.

chapters.title: A Cartographer's Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya outbargains the Pale King: her soul for her life's work — maps that would render every unmapped realm, including his, knowable and thus conquerable by rivals. He cannot refuse the leverage. Emotional beat: intellect as the sharpest blade.

chapters.title: Stars Returned
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The caged stars are released and blaze back into the sky; the contract burns to ash; the party flees the collapsing court with Bramblehoof freed of his thorns. Emotional beat: triumph laced with exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Valley, Rewarded
chapters.summary: Dagny's POV. Home again, the party confronts the saboteur — the valley elder who feared magic more than theft — and chooses restoration over vengeance, rebuilding the wards together. Emotional beat: forgiveness as foundation.

chapters.title: Maps of What Comes Next
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya begins a new atlas — of realms mapped with companions instead of alone — as the stars shine over a valley that chose to let magic back in. Emotional beat: belonging earned, journey continuing.
